document_check.note: Zhang L, Wang Q, Wang X, Fu C, Zhang X, Li X, Wang Z, Zhu D. Association of birth weight, midlife obesity, and transition patterns with mild cognitive impairment and brain MRI indices: a prospective population-based study. J Affect Disord 2025;380:384-393. UK Biobank, the same ICD-10 MCI codes and the same research group as P-648. Matches the review's Zhang et al. 2025c.

cited_result: Incidence of ICD-10-coded MCI (F06.7, G31.8, R41) among 200,726 UK Biobank participants over a mean 13.1 years: 3272 cases (1.6%). The figure is obtained only by summing the Table 2 category counts (377 + 2390 + 505); the paper does not state an overall incidence.
tool_reason: The cited result is an incidence proportion, so the JBI checklist for prevalence and incidence studies applies. The paper's exposure-outcome hazard ratios (birth weight, central obesity) are not what the review cites.

domains.domain: 1. Sample frame appropriate to the target population
domains.rationale: This is a volunteer cohort aged 40 to 70 that the authors describe as predominantly White with limited generalisability.

signalling.question: Was the sample frame appropriate to address the target population?
signalling.quote: the participants in the UK Biobank were predominantly white, which might limit the generalizability of our findings to other ethnicities or populations.

domains.rationale: The sample is a complete-case subset (about 40% of the more than 502,000 cohort), restricted to people with self-reported birth weight and complete covariates. The authors did compare included with excluded participants (supplementary Table S1) and report mostly similar features apart from sex; the exclusion counts are in a figure not reproduced in the text.

signalling.question: Were study participants sampled in an appropriate way?
signalling.quote: A prospective design was adopted based on participants with no MCI at baseline, and had no missing on key covariates. Finally, 200,726 people were included in this prospective analysis.

signalling.question: Were included and excluded participants compared?
signalling.quote: Most features were consistent between the included and excluded people, although the excluded group had a higher proportion of male individuals (Table S1).

domains.rationale: With 200,726 participants, precision is not a concern.

signalling.question: Was the sample size adequate?
signalling.quote: Overall, 200,726 participants were included in the analysis

domains.rationale: Age, sex, ethnicity and a full baseline table by exposure category are reported.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: with a mean (SD) age at baseline of 54.8 years (SD 8.1), and 61.7 % of them were females. The majority of them (96.7 %) were white individuals.

domains.rationale: Outcomes were ascertained by hospital and death-registry linkage for every included participant.

signalling.question: Was the data analysis conducted with sufficient coverage of the identified sample?
signalling.quote: Individual data were linked to hospital data and national death registries from England, Scotland, and Wales (Gong et al. 2021) to determine the date of the first diagnosis of MCI after the baseline assessment.

domains.domain: 6. Valid methods for identification of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI was identified from three ICD-10 codes (including the symptom code R41) in health records. The paper asserts outcome adjudication but gives no procedure and no validation of these codes for MCI.

signalling.question: Were valid methods used for the identification of the condition?
signalling.quote: The International Classification of Diseases 10th revision (ICD-10) F06.7, G31.8 and R41 codes were used to identify participants with MCI if one or more of these codes were recorded as a primary or secondary diagnosis in the health records. Outcome adjudication for MCI was done by the UK Biobank Outcome Adjudication team.

domains.domain: 7. Condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all
domains.rationale: The same linked-record ascertainment and censoring rule applied to all participants.

signalling.question: Was the condition measured in a standard, reliable way for all participants?
signalling.quote: Follow-up was censored on January 1, 2022, or at the time of MCI diagnosis or death, whichever occurred first.

domains.rationale: No overall incidence, confidence interval or person-time rate is reported; only per-category case proportions are given. The Table 2 denominator (200,766) disagrees with the text (200,726).
No response rate or handling of non-response is reported.

signalling.question: Was the response rate adequate, and if not, was the low response rate managed appropriately?
signalling.quote: Searched for response rate, number invited, participation proportion, healthy-volunteer effect and weighting. None is reported.

overall: High (JBI prevalence under this review's rule: 'valid methods for identification of the condition' (item 6) and 'appropriate statistical analysis' (item 8) are both No).
overall_rationale: The incidence rests on unvalidated, broad ICD codes in linked health records. It comes from a volunteer complete-case subset, is not reported as an overall estimate with a confidence interval, and has an inconsistent denominator. Items 6 and 8 at No make the rating high.

applicability.rationale: This is a predominantly White UK volunteer cohort aged 40-70 with hospital-record ascertainment. The figure describes coded ascertainment in this cohort, which is how the review scopes it.
